title: Drinking on the bands
summary: He started drinking in the Scott band, and some musicians could still perform while others could not; Teagarden's wife managed the band.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: In those days--we're talking really about 1942 and '43, in those days, I gather that the recreation on the band was drinking as opposed to dope.

Right. That's when I started drinking, when I joined the Teagarden band--no, it wasn't when I joined the Teagarden band, it was when I joined the Raymond Scott band. Everybody pulled their own bottle under their coats; I had never seen this before, every guy in the band with his own quart of whiskey, my god, so I went out and bought mine and I started to drink with everybody else.
The miraculous thing is, looking back, is that some of these guys were such good drinkers
What do you mean by good drinkers?
They were able to at least perform after drinking predigious amounts of booze.
Right; fantastic. But past a certain point--I don't know how they could tell what that point was--some of them knew just how far they could take it, which is what you're saying.
But guys like Stirling they took it passed the point of being able to perform.
How did the managers react to this, were they all the time running around yelling and screaming to stop it? They were, after all, responsible to the money.
Jack's manager was his wife and she drank as much as he did.
That was also part of Jack's trademark, I guess, his drinking.
